predecessors.name: Kingdom of France
predecessors.text: the lordship of Bourbon (Bourbonnais), whose Sires de Bourbon ran from 913 to 1327 and which 'In 1327, King Charles (le Bel) elevated ... to the status of a duchy'

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: the Bourbon lands of Henry III of Navarre on his accession as Henry IV on 2 August 1589; the Bourbon duchy itself had been sequestered in 1523 and merged into the royal domain in 1531

rulers.name: John I
rulers.title: Duke of Bourbon; Duke of Auvergne from 1416

rulers.name: Charles III
rulers.title: Duke of Bourbon (duke from 1505 by marriage; table end 1523)

rulers.name: Charles of Bourbon, Duke of Vendome
rulers.title: head of the Bourbon-Vendome branch, the senior branch from 1527

rulers.name: Jeanne III of Navarre and Antoine de Bourbon
rulers.title: joint rulers of Navarre from 25 May 1555

rulers.name: Henry III of Navarre (Henry IV of France)
rulers.title: King of Navarre; King of France from 2 August 1589

ledger.x: 1327: King Charles (le Bel) raises the Bourbonnais to a duchy for Louis I.
1327: La Marche comes to the Bourbons.
1341: La Marche leaves the ducal domain for the cadet line.
ledger.cp: County of La Marche (James I of Bourbon)

ledger.x: 1372: Louis II becomes Count of Forez by marriage.
1400: Louis II acquires the lordship of Beaujeu.
1400: Louis II acquires the northern Dombes with the lordship of Beaujeu ('acquired the northern part of the Dombes, together with the lordship of Beaujeu').
ledger.cp: Northern Dombes (holders not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1402: Louis II buys the southern Dombes.
1416: the Dukes of Bourbon become Dukes of Auvergne.
ledger.cp: Duchy of Auvergne (John, Duke of Berry)

ledger.x: 1488: La Marche joins the ducal domain when Peter II becomes Duke of Bourbon (Duke of Bourbon table: 1488-1503).
ledger.cp: County of La Marche (Peter II of Bourbon)

ledger.x: 10 May 1505: Charles de Bourbon (Montpensier) marries Suzanne de Bourbon and the ducal lands pass to him (duke 1505-1523, Duke of Bourbon table).
August 1523: Francis I sequesters the Bourbon lands.
1527: the senior line ends and the Bourbon-Vendome branch becomes the senior one.
1527: the dossier passes to the Bourbon-Vendome branch and its duchy of Vendome.
25 May 1555: Jeanne III and Antoine of Bourbon become joint rulers of the Albret domain, Bearn among it.
1555: Foix comes with Jeanne's inheritance (Foix is in the page's list of her lands); Cliopatria's County of Foix row also ends in 1555.
1555: the rest of the Albret inheritance.
ledger.cp: Kingdom of Navarre and the House of Albret (Henry II of Navarre)

ledger.x: 2 August 1589: Henry III of Navarre becomes Henry IV of France and his Bourbon titles merge into the crown.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Louis II led royal armies in Poitou and Guyenne to recover lands lost after the Treaty of Brétigny (1360): he took Limoges with the Duke of Berry in 1371 and strongholds in Rouergue, Poitou and Touraine in 1374; the Truce of Leulinghem followed in 1389.

wars.name: Charles III's campaigns for Charles V
wars.outcome: After the sequestration of August 1523 Charles III fled France, helped repel a French attempt on Milan, led an invasion of Provence that stalled before Marseille and fought at Pavia, where Francis I was captured; he died at the Sack of Rome on 6 May 1527.

certainty.note: Feudal and apanage lands with no survey or treaty line in the pages opened; Cliopatria's polygons for the Bourbonnais and its additions are approximate (Allier only 88% covered).
